assumptions: Compatible overhangs anneal and ligate; blunt ends join only when allowed.
Ends are as the digest or end treatments left them.
limits: All possible products are enumerated, not their relative yield.
Digest-then-ligate is a different reaction from one-pot restriction-ligation (restriction_ligate).
bio.jane/contract.question: What products do these fragments make when their ends are ligated (after any per-fragment digest)?

description: Ligate fragments by their overhangs (pydna ligation_assembly) — sticky, optionally blunt. Each input may be digested by its own enzymes first, which is the digest → ligate hand-off. Emits the first product as a NEW record.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

allow_partial_overlap.description: allow partially overlapping sticky ends. Advanced.

blunt.description: allow blunt-end joins as well as sticky.

end_origins.description: what MADE each input's ends, positionally — this fixes the 5'-phosphate before any treatment. Leave empty for `unspecified`, which is treated as phosphorylated and reproduces a run with no end chemistry at all. Advanced.

end_treatments.description: the phosphatase or kinase applied to each input AFTER it was made, positionally. Dephosphorylating the vector is what stops it self-ligating; a junction with no 5'-phosphate on either strand forms no bond and the product is dropped. Advanced.

enzymes.description: digest every input with these enzymes before ligating. Left unset, the run uses your active enzyme collection.

fill_in.description: positional booleans: fill that input's 5' overhangs with Klenow after its digest, so its cut ends join blunt (needs `blunt`). Each join then reports the bases the fill-in added. Advanced.

fragment_indices.description: which band to take from each input's digest, positionally (0 = first fragment). Leave empty to use every fragment — which frequently yields no product, exactly as at the bench.

fragments.description: the fragments to ligate — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or name library documents.

include_subject.description: also include the node's subject as a fragment.

name: ligate_fragments

junctions.description: the junctions formed, with the overhang each was made by

layout.description: where each piece and join sits ON the product: the spans the map draws

nickedJunctions.description: indices of junctions left NICKED by a missing 5'-phosphate on one strand — the product still transforms and is repaired in vivo. Empty when every junction sealed

record.description: the first ligation product, as a record
